title: A goal reports which required variables are unset, and the repository lists their names in .env.example
description:
SPIDR grandchild C of task-72b22fcf9da54b3b91dabf5b7392aff1 (architect-aa54e231, 2026-09-05). Owns the parent's DoD 3 and 4. dependsOn grandchild B task-fd2d438f29d64830a2bd6110f2ded78b, which adds the field this row READS - without it there are no names to report, and the parent's DoD 3 is unsatisfiable (measured: no variable-name field exists on a deployment requirement anywhere).

Deliberately does NOT depend on grandchild A: the unset report needs the NAMES of what is set, which the existing read already returns as metadata (apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-store.ts `readEnvironmentVariables`), not the plaintext values A delivers. A and C can run in parallel.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: reading the required names off the approved contract, reporting which are unset for a given environment, and putting those names into the repository's `.env.example`.

`.env.example` ALREADY EXISTS AND ALREADY CARRIES VALUES - this is the trap and it is measured, not guessed. It is generated by the CONTROLLED-PROFILE generator, not by the node lander the parent's description names:
  apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:204 maps `.env.example` to an ENV_EXAMPLE template, whose current content includes a real placeholder value (`POSTGRES_PASSWORD=...`, and README copy at :113 telling the operator to `cp .env.example .env   # then replace every CHANGE_ME`).
  apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:32 pins the file by SHA256 in a golden manifest - editing the template MOVES that hash and the pin must move with it.
  apps/daemon/src/repository/deployment/deployment-infrastructure-generator.test.ts:305-306 READS a placeholder back out of `.env.example` with `/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=(\S+)/`, so a rewrite that drops the placeholder line reds a test in a different directory.
So this row EXTENDS an existing generated file with a NAMES-ONLY section; it does not create one, and it must not break the profile's own placeholder contract. Decide deliberately whether the required names go in the same file or an adjacent one, and say which and why.

CONCURRENCY WARNING: `controlled-profile-generator.ts` and its assets were being actively built by another session on 2026-09-05 (the ASSEMBLY HALF and the lockfile-asset mint). Re-measure at claim, expect the golden manifest hash to have moved, and never revert peer work.

NOT IN SCOPE: the plaintext delivery and the spawn merge (grandchild A); the Environments screen and the goal's unset count in the browser (the parent's child 3 - this row's report is a daemon-side read, not UI).

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
definitionOfDone: The required variable names are read from the APPROVED CONTRACT's deployment requirements (the field grandchild B added), never from a hand-kept list. Assert the read against a contract fixture carrying names, and assert that a contract with no names yields an empty required set rather than throwing.

A goal reports which required variables are UNSET for a given environment. Assert the exact unset SET for a goal with two required names where one is set - set equality, not toContain, and assert the SET one is absent from the report so the arm fails if the report simply echoes the requirement list.

`.env.example` carries every required NAME and NO VALUE for them. Assert the generated bytes contain each required name and that no required name is followed by a value; this file is committed and pushed through the repository, so a value here is a value published.

THE EXISTING PROFILE CONTRACT SURVIVES: the profile's own `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` placeholder is still present and still matches `/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=(\S+)/`, because apps/daemon/src/repository/deployment/deployment-infrastructure-generator.test.ts:305-306 reads it back. Assert it, and move the golden SHA256 pin at controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:32 to the new measured value rather than deleting the pin.

A contract with NO deployment-variable names generates the `.env.example` byte-identically to today - assert byte-identity, so this feature cannot change the profile for every project that does not use it.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: NAMES ONLY. `.env.example` is committed and pushed to the project's repository; a value written there is a value published. This is the single most common way this class of feature leaks.

EXTEND, DO NOT REPLACE, the existing generated `.env.example`. It already carries the profile's own placeholder, another directory's test reads that placeholder back, and a golden SHA256 pins the file.
MOVE THE GOLDEN PIN, NEVER DELETE IT. controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:32 pins .env.example by SHA256; re-measure and update the hash, and never soften the manifest to a looser assertion.
READ NAMES FROM THE APPROVED CONTRACT, never a hand-kept list - that is the whole point of grandchild B.
A PROJECT THAT NAMES NO VARIABLES MUST BE UNCHANGED, asserted as byte-identity of the generated file.
NO UI: the Environments screen and the browser's unset count are the parent's child 3.

THE SHARED-VALIDATOR FACT THAT DECIDES HOW YOU READ. Measured at plan time: `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/gate1-contract-shape.ts:167-173` uses the SAME `requirement` validator for SIX sections — functionalRequirements, nonFunctionalRequirements, securityPrivacyRequirements, technologyRequirements, uxAccessibilityRequirements and deploymentRequirements. So B either put the field on ALL SIX or gave `deploymentRequirements` its own validator. Which one B chose changes this row: if all six carry it, you MUST filter to deployment requirements or you will collect variable names a security requirement happened to declare.

AND DO NOT READ THROUGH `gate1Requirements()`. That helper (:182-189) FLATTENS all six sections into one array, so an entry's section of origin is lost and a deployment requirement is indistinguishable from a technology one. Read `revision.deploymentRequirements` directly. This is the single easiest way to get this row silently wrong — the flattened helper is the obvious thing to reach for and it compiles fine.

implementationPlan.description:
RED ARMS FIRST for the required-names read and the unset report, in a new test beside the module you create in step 3. Write them and watch them FAIL.

THE UNSET SET IS A SET DIFFERENCE, and both sides are measured: the REQUIRED names come from the approved contract's `deploymentRequirements` (B's field), and the SET names come from the existing store read — `readEnvironmentVariables` returns `EnvironmentVariableRead[]`, each `{ fingerprintSha256, isSet: true, name, updatedAt }` (apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-contracts.ts:118-123). It returns only variables that ARE set, each carrying its `name`, so unset = required MINUS the names it returns. No value is read anywhere in this row.

Arms:
  1. THE DoD-2 CASE, exactly as specified: two required names, one of them set. Assert the unset set by SET EQUALITY, and separately assert the SET one is ABSENT from the report. Without that second assertion the arm passes for a report that simply echoes the requirement list — which is the most likely wrong implementation.
  2. NO NAMES IS EMPTY, NOT AN ERROR. A contract whose deployment requirements name no variables yields an empty required set and an empty unset set — it must not throw and must not report everything as unset.
  3. WRONG-SECTION NAMES ARE NOT COLLECTED. Build a contract where a NON-deployment requirement (say a technologyRequirement) carries variable names, and assert they do NOT appear in the required set. If B put the field on all six sections this arm is the one that catches a read through `gate1Requirements()`; if B gave deploymentRequirements its own validator, write the arm anyway — it pins the intended scope against a later widening.
  4. AN ENVIRONMENT WITH NOTHING SET reports every required name as unset.

Assert against the production read, never a helper that re-derives the difference.

implementationPlan.description:
THE REQUIRED-NAMES READ AND THE UNSET REPORT — a new focused module under apps/daemon/src/environment/ (or the deployment area if that reads better; say which and why), plus its one-line `.js` bridge, copying the shape of apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-store.js.

Export two things and keep them separate:
  - `requiredVariableNames(revision)` — reads `revision.deploymentRequirements` DIRECTLY (never `gate1Requirements()`, which flattens six sections and loses the origin), collects B's field, dedupes, and returns names in a stable sorted order. Sorted because this feeds `.env.example` in step 4, and an unstable order would move the golden SHA256 pin on every unrelated contract edit.
  - `unsetVariableNames(required, read)` — the set difference against the names `readEnvironmentVariables` returns. Keep it a pure function over its two arguments so it is testable without a store, and so the store read stays the single seam that touches durable bytes.

NO VALUE IS READ, RETURNED OR LOGGED anywhere in this module. This row works entirely in names: `EnvironmentVariableRead` carries `name` and `fingerprintSha256` and no value, and grandchild A owns the only value-returning path. If you find yourself needing a value here, stop — the requirement was misread.

Handle the shapes a real contract presents: a requirement whose field is absent, an empty list, a duplicate name across two requirements (dedupe), and a name that is not a plausible environment variable. For that last case decide deliberately whether to drop it or surface it, and say which in the step note — do not silently pass through whatever the contract text held.

Keep the module well under 250 lines.

implementationPlan.description:
`.env.example` CARRIES THE NAMES, AND NOTHING ELSE. EXTEND the existing generated file — do not create one and do not rewrite it.

What is already there, measured: `apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:204` maps `.env.example` to an `ENV_EXAMPLE` template that already carries the profile's OWN placeholder (`POSTGRES_PASSWORD=...`), and README copy at :113 tells the operator `cp .env.example .env   # then replace every CHANGE_ME`. The docker-compose template consumes `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}`.

THREE THINGS MUST ALL HOLD AFTERWARDS:
  (a) Every required name from step 3 appears in the file, as a NAME ONLY — no value, no placeholder value, no CHANGE_ME token beside it. Assert that no required name is followed by a value. This file is committed and pushed into the project's repository, so a value written here is a value published; that is the single most common way this class of feature leaks.
  (b) THE PROFILE'S OWN PLACEHOLDER SURVIVES UNCHANGED. `apps/daemon/src/repository/deployment/deployment-infrastructure-generator.test.ts:305-306` reads it back out with `/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=(\S+)/` from a DIFFERENT directory, so dropping or reformatting that line reds a test that never mentions this row. The profile's placeholder and the contract's required names are two different things living in one file — keep them visibly separate (a commented section for the contract-derived names is the obvious shape) and say in the step note why they are not merged.
  (c) THE GOLDEN PIN MOVES, IT DOES NOT SOFTEN. `controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:32` pins `.env.example` by SHA256 in the golden manifest. Re-measure the hash and update the literal. Never replace the pin with a looser assertion to avoid re-measuring it — the pin is what makes the manifest evidence.

AND THE NO-OP CASE, which is DoD 5 and the reason this feature cannot regress every project: a contract naming NO variables must generate `.env.example` BYTE-IDENTICALLY to today. Assert byte-identity, and confirm the golden hash for that case is the pre-existing one — if the no-name path moves the hash, the extension is unconditional and must be made conditional.
implementationPlan.note:
THE REJECTED DEFECT IS FIXED, RED-FIRST. QA issues 1, 2 and 4 all resolve here.

ARMS WRITTEN FIRST AND WATCHED FAIL against the unfixed production surface at HEAD:

    - "never re-declares a name the profile section already assigns": `expected [ 'POSTGRES_USER', ...(6) ] to deeply equal [ 'POSTGRES_USER', ...(4) ]` — six assignment keys where four are distinct, i.e. `DATABASE_URL` and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` each emitted twice. That is QA's probe reproduced as an arm.
    - "emits the profile's own bytes when EVERY required name is one the profile assigns": Object.is inequality against the untouched profile file.

THE FIX (controlled-profile-root-templates.ts). New `ENV_EXAMPLE_PROFILE_ASSIGNED_NAMES`, a `ReadonlySet<string>` DERIVED from `ENV_EXAMPLE_PROFILE_LINES` — each line split at its FIRST `=`, comment lines and non-assignments dropped — exactly as QA required, never a hand-listed constant, because the profile's lines are editable and a hand list would drift the moment someone adds a variable. `envExample` filters the contract's names through it before sorting.

THE COLLISION RULE IS STATED IN THE CODE, in the new doc-comment, with its reason and the rejected alternative: the PROFILE'S LINE WINS and the contract's declaration is dropped, because the requirement is already SATISFIED by that line (the operator gets a value to edit, which is strictly more than a bare name). The alternative — contract wins, profile line deleted — would move the `/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=(\S+)/` read-back at deployment-infrastructure-generator.test.ts:305-306 and strip a working placeholder. That is QA's expected option one.

ORDER MATTERS AND IS DOCUMENTED: the exclusion runs BEFORE the `names.length === 0` decision. A contract whose names ALL collide otherwise gets a heading announcing a section with no lines under it. Filtering first makes the empty case and the fully-colliding case the same case, and the second new arm pins it by BYTE-IDENTITY against the untouched profile file — `withNames(["POSTGRES_PASSWORD"])` and `withNames(["DATABASE_URL","POSTGRES_USER","PORT"])` both equal `tree("alpha-product")`'s bytes.

ANTI-VACUITY, because an over-filtering bug would satisfy both collision arms: the same arm asserts `withNames(["DATABASE_URL","APP_SECRET_NAME"])` still contains `\nAPP_SECRET_NAME=\n`. Dropping every name reds it.

FILE-WIDE, NOT JUST THE TWO NAMES, per QA: the arm collects every non-comment `KEY=` line in the emitted file and asserts `keys` equals its own dedupe, so ANY duplicate key anywhere reds it; then it asserts each colliding key keeps its PROFILE value (`DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:CHANGE_ME@localhost:5432/app`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=CHANGE_ME`), which is the effective-value claim DoD 4 was only holding textually before.

QA ISSUE 4 (heading copy false for a colliding name) IS RESOLVED BY THE SAME CHANGE rather than by rewording: no colliding name is listed under the heading any more, so "none has a default and none has a placeholder" is now true of every line beneath it. The emitted heading bytes are therefore UNCHANGED, which is why `GOLDEN_ENV_EXAMPLE_WITH_NAMES` did not have to move.

BOTH GOLDEN PINS UNMOVED, as QA predicted: the fixture `REQUIRED = ["APP_SECRET_NAME","DATABASE_URL_EXTRA","SESSION_SIGNING_KEY"]` collides with nothing, so the with-names hash `a391d228...` still matches, and the no-names pin at :32 (`79bcb754...`) still matches.
